1  JUDGMENT

The above Appeal is filed against the common order dated 05.11.2021 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Subordinate Court, Tiruppur in M.C.O.P.No.1255 and 1267 of 2000.
2.Brief facts of the case are, as follows:

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Subordinate Court, Tiruppur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On 26.10.2000, when the deceased Sivasami was riding his motor cycle on Tiruppur-Avinasi Road, near Anaiputhur, around 12.30 a.m., a Jeep bearing Registration No.TN 57 B 5874 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against him and immediately the injured Sivasami was taken to Tiruppur Government Hospital.
However, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
According to the claimants in M.C.O.P.No.1255 of 2000, the deceased Sivasami was working as a Supervisor in SSM International and was earning a sum of Rs.5000/- as monthly income.
They filed a claim petition in M.C.O.P.No.1255 of 2000 seeking a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- as compensation for the death of the deceased.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
3.Before the Tribunal, on behalf of the claimants in M.C.O.P.No.1255 of 2000, 12 documents were marked as Exs.P1 to P8 and no witness was examined.
On behalf of the respondents, 5 documents were marked as Exs.R1 to R5 and no witness was examined.

The Tribunal, after hearing both sides and examining the material documents available on record, awarded a sum of Rs.6,19,000/- as compensation to the claimants, as tabulated hereunder:
 Head Award (Rs.)
 Loss of earning 6,12,000.00  Funeral expenses 2,000.00  Loss of consortium & 5,000.00  Loss of Love and affection  Total 6,19,000.
4.Challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in M.C.O.P.No.1255 of 2000,
that it is inordinately high, the claimants have come up with the present Appeal.

5.Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is certainly on the higher side and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/05/2025 02:51:41 pm ) it is liable to be interfered with.
Though notice has been served and the names of the respondents are printed in the cause list, there is no representation on their behalf.

K.Subramaniam vs Tmt.Sakuntala on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147227668/
2 6.Though, according to the claimants, the deceased Sivasami was earning a sum of Rs.5000/- per month by working as a Supervisor in a Private Company, the Tribunal, taking into account the economic index prevailing then, has fixed his monthly income at Rs.4,500/- and by applying the multiplier of 17 as per the Second Schedule to Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, has arrived at a sum of Rs.9,18,000/- (Rs.4,500/- x 12 x 17 = Rs.9,18,000/-)
as compensation towards loss of earning

. The Tribunal, after deducting one-third towards his personal expenses, has arrived at a sum of Rs.6,12,000/- (Rs.9,18,000/- - Rs.3,06,000/-, i.e. one third of Rs.9,18,000/-) as compensation under the said head.
7.The appellants have disputed that the Tribunal has wrongly applied the multiplier of 17 while arriving at the compensation towards loss of earning.

However, on examining the material documents https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/05/2025 02:51:41 pm ) available on record, this Court holds that the Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier of 17, as the deceased was aged only 32 years at the time of accident which took place on 26.10.2000.
Hence, this Court does not find any reason to interfere with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of earning.
Also, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the compensation awarded under the heads funeral expenses and loss of consortium together with loss of love and affection.
8.In view of the above, the common order dated 05.11.2001 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Subordinate Court, Tiruppur in M.C.O.P.No.1255 and 1267 of 2000, is confirmed.

29/05/2025 02:51:41 pm ) issued by the Tribunal with regard to the mode of payment of compensation remain unaltered.
10.In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
